AIGEN_grade5_005fc3f8-e2b5-4c4a-85d9-7ce.q: Neha and her dad are driving from Hyderabad to Vijayawada for a cricket match. The total distance is 270 kilometres. They start at 7:00 a m. For the first 90 kilometres, they drive at 60 kilometres per hour. Then they stop at a dhaba for a 30-minute chai break. For the next 120 kilometres, they drive at 80 kilometres per hour. Finally, for the last stretch, they drive at 60 kilometres per hour. At what time do they reach Vijayawada?
hints: Break the journey into parts: find the time for each driving segment and don't forget the chai break! Then add all the times to 7:00 a m.
First, figure out the distance of the last stretch: Total distance minus the first two parts. Then use Time equals Distance divided by Speed for each segment.

Here's a similar problem: Suppose someone travels 40 kilometres at 40 kilometres per hour, which is 1 hour, takes a 15-minute break, then 60 kilometres at 30 kilometres per hour, which is 2 hours, then 20 kilometres at 20 kilometres per hour, which is 1 hour. Total time equals 1 plus 0.25 plus 2 plus 1, which is 4.25 hours, which is 4 hours 15 minutes. If they started at 8:00 a m, they arrive at 12 15 p m.
steps: Find the distance of the last stretch. 270 minus 90 minus 120 equals 60 kilometres.
Find the time for the first segment: 90 kilometres at 60 kilometres per hour. Time 1 equals 90 divided by 60, which is 1.5 hours, which is 1 hour 30 minutes.
Don't forget the chai break at the dhaba! Break equals 30 minutes.
Find the time for the second segment: 120 kilometres at 80 kilometres per hour. Time 2 equals 120 divided by 80, which is 1.5 hours, which is 1 hour 30 minutes.
Find the time for the last segment: 60 kilometres at 60 kilometres per hour. Time 3 equals 60 divided by 60, which is 1 hour.
Add up all the times: driving plus break. 1 hour 30 minutes, plus 30 minutes, plus 1 hour 30 minutes, plus 1 hour, equals 4 hours 30 minutes.
Add the total time to the start time of 7:00 a m. 7:00 a m plus 4 hours 30 minutes equals 11 30 a m.

AIGEN_grade5_008aeb36-e7d1-453c-8ac2-dd1.q: Priya and her family are taking the Shatabdi Express from Chennai to Bangalore. The train departs at 6:00 a m. It covers the first 120 kilometres at 80 kilometres per hour, then stops at Vellore station for 30 minutes. After that, it covers the remaining 240 kilometres at 120 kilometres per hour. At what time does the train arrive in Bangalore?
hints: Break the journey into three parts: the first stretch, the stop, and the second stretch. Find the time for each part separately, then add them all up!
Start by finding the time for the first 120 kilometres: Time equals Distance divided by Speed, which is 120 divided by 80. What does that give you?

Here's a similar problem: A bus leaves at 8:00 a m, travels 60 kilometres at 30 kilometres per hour, stops for 15 minutes, then travels 90 kilometres at 45 kilometres per hour. Time for first part equals 60 divided by 30, which is 2 hours. Stop equals 15 minutes. Time for second part equals 90 divided by 45, which is 2 hours. Total equals 2 hours plus 15 minutes plus 2 hours, which is 4 hours 15 minutes. Arrival equals 12 15 p m. Now try the original problem the same way!
steps: Find the time for the first stretch of 120 kilometres at 80 kilometres per hour. Time 1 equals 120 divided by 80, which is 1.5 hours, which is 1 hour 30 minutes.
The train stops at Vellore for 30 minutes. Don't forget to include this! Stop time equals 30 minutes.
Find the time for the second stretch of 240 kilometres at 120 kilometres per hour. Time 2 equals 240 divided by 120, which is 2 hours.
Add up all three parts to get the total journey time. Total time equals 1 hour 30 minutes plus 30 minutes plus 2 hours, which is 4 hours.
The train departs at 6:00 a m. Add 4 hours to find the arrival time. 6:00 a m plus 4 hours equals 10:00 a m.
The train arrives in Bangalore at 10:00 a m!

AIGEN_grade5_0275ee67-deaa-41e1-b4b9-ad8.q: Ravi takes an auto-rickshaw from his home to the railway station, which is 18 kilometres away. The auto travels at 36 kilometres per hour for the first half of the distance and at 24 kilometres per hour for the second half. How many minutes does the entire trip take?
hints: Think about it in two parts, find the time for each half of the journey separately, then add them up!
The first half is 9 kilometres at 36 kilometres per hour. Use Time equals Distance divided by Speed to find the time for this part.

Here's a similar problem: A bike goes 10 kilometres at 20 kilometres per hour and then 10 kilometres at 40 kilometres per hour. Time for first part equals 10 divided by 20, which is 0.5 hours, which is 30 minutes. Time for second part equals 10 divided by 40, which is 0.25 hours, which is 15 minutes. Total equals 30 plus 15, which is 45 minutes.
steps: The total distance is 18 kilometres, so each half is 9 kilometres.
Time for the first half: Distance divided by Speed. 9 divided by 36 equals one quarter of an hour, which is 15 minutes.
Time for the second half: Distance divided by Speed. 9 divided by 24 equals 3 over 8 of an hour, which is 22.5 minutes.
Total time equals 15 plus 22.5, which is 37.5 minutes.

AIGEN_grade5_10d2ce3d-f46f-486a-8d20-0df.q: Deepa and her brother Arjun start cycling from their home to their grandmother's house, which is 30 kilometres away. Deepa cycles the entire distance at a constant speed of 10 kilometres per hour. Arjun starts at the same time but cycles at 15 kilometres per hour. However, after reaching grandmother's house, Arjun realizes he forgot the box of sweets at home! He immediately turns around, cycles back home at 15 kilometres per hour, picks up the sweets, and cycles back to grandmother's house at 15 kilometres per hour. By how many hours does Arjun arrive, the second time, after Deepa?
hints: Think about the total distance Arjun travels in all. He goes to grandma's house, back home, and then to grandma's house again!
First, find the total distance Arjun covers: 30 kilometres plus 30 kilometres plus 30 kilometres equals 90 kilometres. Then find his total time at 15 kilometres per hour.

Here's a similar problem: Sam walks 20 kilometres at 5 kilometres per hour. His friend Jay walks 20 kilometres to the destination at 10 kilometres per hour, walks back 20 kilometres, then walks 20 kilometres again, all at 10 kilometres per hour. Jay's total distance equals 60 kilometres, Jay's time equals 60 divided by 10, which is 6 hours. Sam's time equals 20 divided by 5, which is 4 hours. Jay arrives 6 minus 4, which is 2 hours after Sam.
steps: Find the time Deepa takes to reach grandmother's house. Deepa's time equals 30 divided by 10, which is 3 hours.

Find the total distance Arjun travels. He cycles from home to grandma's, 30 kilometres, then from grandma's back home, 30 kilometres, then from home to grandma's again, 30 kilometres. Arjun's total distance equals 30 plus 30 plus 30, which is 90 kilometres.
Find the total time Arjun takes. He cycles the entire 90 kilometres at 15 kilometres per hour. Arjun's time equals 90 divided by 15, which is 6 hours.
Find how many hours later Arjun arrives compared to Deepa. 6 minus 3 equals 3 hours.
So Arjun arrives 3 hours after Deepa. That's the cost of forgetting the sweets!

AIGEN_grade5_18327336-63b9-4b85-97e2-d90.q: Neha's family is traveling by car from Pune to a picnic spot. They drive at 40 kilometres per hour for the first 2 hours. Then they stop for chai for 30 minutes. After the break, they drive at 60 kilometres per hour for 1 hour to reach the picnic spot. What is their average speed for the entire journey, including the chai break?
hints: Remember, average speed equals total distance divided by total time. Don't forget to include the chai break in the total time!
First, find the distance covered in each part: Distance equals Speed times Time. Then add up all distances and all times, including the break.

Here's a similar problem: A boy walks 10 kilometres in 2 hours, rests for 1 hour, then walks 8 kilometres in 2 hours. Total distance equals 10 plus 8, which is 18 kilometres. Total time equals 2 plus 1 plus 2, which is 5 hours. Average speed equals 18 divided by 5, which is 3.6 kilometres per hour. Notice how the rest time is included!
steps: Find the distance covered in the first part. Distance 1 equals 40 times 2, which is 80 kilometres.
Find the distance covered in the second part, after the chai break. Distance 2 equals 60 times 1, which is 60 kilometres.
Find the total distance. Total Distance equals 80 plus 60, which is 140 kilometres.
Find the total time, including the 30-minute, 0.5 hour, chai break. Total Time equals 2 plus 0.5 plus 1, which is 3.5 hours.
Calculate the average speed. Average Speed equals 140 divided by 3.5, which is 40 kilometres per hour.

AIGEN_grade5_1f368230-2fc1-4206-bff3-182.q: Deepa and her mother are taking a boat ride on Dal Lake in Srinagar. The boatman rows at 6 kilometres per hour for 20 minutes to reach an island, and then rows back along the same route at 4 kilometres per hour. How much total time does the entire boat ride, going and coming back, take?
hints: First, figure out the distance to the island using the speed and time for the onward trip. Then use that distance to find the return time!
Distance equals Speed times Time. The boat goes at 6 kilometres per hour for 20 minutes. Convert 20 minutes to hours first: 20 minutes equals one third of an hour.

Here's a similar problem: A cyclist rides at 10 kilometres per hour for 30 minutes to reach a park. She returns at 5 kilometres per hour. Distance to park equals 10 times 30 divided by 60, which is 5 kilometres. Return time equals 5 divided by 5, which is 1 hour, which is 60 minutes. Total time equals 30 plus 60, which is 90 minutes.
steps: Find the distance to the island. Speed equals 6 kilometres per hour, Time equals 20 minutes, which is one third of an hour. Distance equals 6 times one third, which is 2 kilometres.
Find the time for the return trip. The distance is the same, 2 kilometres, but the speed is 4 kilometres per hour. Return time equals 2 divided by 4, which is half an hour, which is 30 minutes.
Add both times together to get the total time for the boat ride. Total time equals 20 plus 30, which is 50 minutes.
The entire boat ride takes 50 minutes!

AIGEN_grade5_1fe16fb0-b0a5-4b97-b6d6-494.q: Ravi takes a boat ride across a river during a village fair in Kerala. The boat travels 3 kilometres downstream, with the current, at a speed of 15 kilometres per hour and then returns the same 3 kilometres upstream, against the current, at a speed of 5 kilometres per hour. What is the average speed of the entire boat trip?
hints: Average speed isn't just the average of the two speeds! Think about the total distance and the total time separately.
First, find the time taken for each part of the trip using Time equals Distance divided by Speed.

Here's a similar problem: A girl walks 4 kilometres at 8 kilometres per hour and then 4 kilometres at 2 kilometres per hour. Total distance equals 8 kilometres. Time for first part equals 4 divided by 8, which is 0.5 hours, time for second part equals 4 divided by 2, which is 2 hours. Total time equals 2.5 hours. Average speed equals 8 divided by 2.5, which is 3.2 kilometres per hour.
steps: Find the total distance of the trip. Total distance equals 3 plus 3, which is 6 kilometres.
Find the time taken to go downstream. Time 1 equals 3 divided by 15, which is 1 over 5 of an hour, which is 12 minutes.
Find the time taken to go upstream. Time 2 equals 3 over 5 of an hour, which is 36 minutes.
Find the total time for the entire trip. Total time equals 1 over 5 plus 3 over 5, which is 4 over 5 of an hour, which is 48 minutes.

Now calculate the average speed using the formula: Average Speed equals Total Distance divided by Total Time. Average speed equals 6 divided by 4 over 5, which is 6 times 5 over 4, which is 30 divided by 4, which is 7.5 kilometres per hour.

AIGEN_grade5_27632c7e-9b71-456a-a6b0-d35.q: Ravi and his grandfather take a boat ride on the Ganges during Chhath Puja. They travel upstream, against the current, at 6 kilometres per hour for 2 hours to reach a temple. After offering prayers for 1 hour, they return downstream, with the current, along the same route at 12 kilometres per hour. What is their average speed for the entire journey, excluding the prayer time?
hints: Average speed isn't just the average of the two speeds! Think: Average Speed equals Total Distance divided by Total Time.
First, find the distance traveled upstream using Distance equals Speed times Time. Then figure out how long the return trip takes.

Here's a similar problem. A cyclist rides 30 kilometres at 10 kilometres per hour, and returns the same 30 kilometres at 15 kilometres per hour. Total distance equals 30 plus 30, which is 60 kilometres. Total time equals 3 plus 2, which is 5 hours. Average speed equals 60 divided by 5, which is 12 kilometres per hour.
steps: Find the distance traveled upstream. They go at 6 kilometres per hour for 2 hours. Distance upstream equals 6 times 2, which is 12 kilometres.
The return trip covers the same distance, 12 kilometres, but downstream at 12 kilometres per hour. Find the time for the return trip. Time downstream equals 12 divided by 12, which is 1 hour.
Calculate the total distance for the entire journey, both ways. Total distance equals 12 plus 12, which is 24 kilometres.
Calculate the total travel time, excluding prayer time, as the question says. Total time equals 2 plus 1, which is 3 hours.
Now find the average speed using the formula. Average speed equals 24 divided by 3, which is 8 kilometres per hour.

AIGEN_grade5_2d6440d7-34f6-4b72-9433-cc2.q: Kavya and her mom take a boat ride during Onam celebrations. The boat travels 18 kilometres downstream, with the current, in 2 hours and then returns the same 18 kilometres upstream, against the current, in 3 hours. What is the boat's average speed for the entire round trip?
hints: Average speed isn't just the average of the two speeds! Think about total distance divided by total time.
First find the total distance, there and back, and the total time taken for the whole trip.

Here's a similar problem. A cyclist rides 30 kilometres in 2 hours, and returns the same 30 kilometres in 3 hours. Total distance equals 30 plus 30, which is 60 kilometres. Total time equals 2 plus 3, which is 5 hours. Average speed equals 60 divided by 5, which is 12 kilometres per hour.
steps: Find the total distance. The boat goes 18 kilometres downstream and 18 kilometres upstream. Total distance equals 18 plus 18, which is 36 kilometres.
Find the total time. It takes 2 hours downstream and 3 hours upstream. Total time equals 2 plus 3, which is 5 hours.
Use the average speed formula: total distance divided by total time. Average speed equals 36 divided by 5, which is 7.2 kilometres per hour.
So Kavya's boat had an average speed of 7.2 kilometres per hour for the whole round trip!

AIGEN_grade5_479772a7-763e-438e-90f0-fd2.q: Deepa and her cousin Riya are visiting a temple fair in Madurai. They take a boat ride across a river that is 600 metres wide. The boat goes across the river at 3 metres per second but the return trip is slower because of the current, so it comes back at 2 metres per second. They make one complete round trip, across and back. What is the average speed of the boat for the entire round trip?
hints: Average speed isn't just the average of the two speeds! Think: Average speed equals Total distance divided by Total time.
First find the total distance, across plus back equals 600 plus 600. Then find the time for each leg separately using Time equals Distance divided by Speed.

Here's a similar problem. A boat crosses a river 60 metres wide at 6 metres per second, and comes back at 3 metres per second. Total distance equals 60 plus 60, which is 120 metres. Time going equals 60 divided by 6, which is 10 seconds, and time returning equals 60 divided by 3, which is 20 seconds, so total time equals 30 seconds. Average speed equals 120 divided by 30, which is 4 metres per second.
steps: Find the total distance for the round trip. Total distance equals 600 plus 600, which is 1200 metres.
Find the time taken to cross the river, going. Time 1 equals 600 divided by 3, which is 200 seconds.
Find the time taken for the return trip, coming back. Time 2 equals 600 divided by 2, which is 300 seconds.
Find the total time for the round trip. Total time equals 200 plus 300, which is 500 seconds.
Now calculate the average speed using Total Distance divided by Total Time. Average speed equals 1200 divided by 500, which is 2.4 metres per second.

AIGEN_grade5_4a0451d9-932e-40a5-b895-2ac.q: Neha and her mom are going by car from Jaipur to Udaipur for a family wedding. The total distance is 400 kilometres. They drive the first half of the total time at 80 kilometres per hour and the second half of the total time at 40 kilometres per hour. What is their average speed for the entire journey?
hints: Be careful! This says half of the time, not half of the distance. When time is split equally, average speed is simpler than you might think!

If the total time is T hours, she drives T over 2 hours at 80 kilometres per hour and T over 2 hours at 40 kilometres per hour. Find the total distance in terms of T, then use Average Speed equals Total Distance divided by Total Time.

Similar problem: A boy walks for 1 hour at 6 kilometres per hour and then 1 hour at 4 kilometres per hour. Total distance equals 6 plus 4, which is 10 kilometres. Total time equals 2 hours. Average speed equals 10 divided by 2, which is 5 kilometres per hour. Notice that when time is split equally, average speed is just 6 plus 4, all divided by 2, which is 5 kilometres per hour!
steps: Let the total time for the journey be T hours. She drives for T over 2 hours at 80 kilometres per hour and T over 2 hours at 40 kilometres per hour.
Distance covered in the first half of the time: d 1 equals 80 times T over 2, which is 40 T kilometres.
Distance covered in the second half of the time: d 2 equals 40 times T over 2, which is 20 T kilometres.
Total distance equals d one plus d two, which is 40 T plus 20 T, which is 60 T kilometres.
Average Speed equals Total Distance divided by Total Time. Average Speed equals 60 T over T, which is 60 kilometres per hour.
When the time is split equally between two speeds, the average speed is simply the arithmetic mean, ordinary average, of the two speeds: 80 plus 40, all divided by 2, which is 60 kilometres per hour.

AIGEN_grade5_4b594e5a-c931-42a0-8c21-513.q: During a school sports day, Priya and Kiran start cycling from school to a park 60 kilometres away at the same time. Priya cycles at a constant speed of 15 kilometres per hour. Kiran cycles the first half of the distance at 10 kilometres per hour and the second half of the distance at 20 kilometres per hour. Who reaches the park first, and by how many minutes?
options: They reach at the same time
hints: Think carefully: when Kiran cycles half the distance at each speed, her average speed is NOT simply the average of 10 and 20. Calculate each person's total time separately!
Start by finding Priya's total time: Time equals Distance divided by Speed, which is 60 divided by 15. Then find Kiran's time for the first 30 kilometres and the next 30 kilometres separately.

Here's a similar problem. Asha walks 24 kilometres at a steady 8 kilometres per hour, so she takes 24 divided by 8, which is 3 hours. Bala walks the first 12 kilometres at 4 kilometres per hour, and the next 12 kilometres at 12 kilometres per hour, so he takes 3 plus 1, which is 4 hours. Asha arrives first, by 4 minus 3, which is 1 hour.
steps: Find Priya's total time. She cycles 60 kilometres at a constant 15 kilometres per hour. Priya's time equals 60 divided by 15, which is 4 hours.
Find Kiran's time for the first half of the distance, 30 kilometres at 10 kilometres per hour. Time 1 equals 30 divided by 10, which is 3 hours.
Find Kiran's time for the second half of the distance, 30 kilometres at 20 kilometres per hour. Time 2 equals 30 divided by 20, which is 1.5 hours.
Find Kiran's total time by adding both parts. Kiran's total time equals 3 plus 1.5, which is 4.5 hours.
Compare: Priya takes 4 hours and Kiran takes 4.5 hours. Priya reaches first! Difference equals 4.5 minus 4, which is 0.5 hours, which is 30 minutes.

So Priya reaches the park 30 minutes before Kiran. The key insight is that Kiran spends more time at the slower speed, 3 hours at 10 kilometres per hour, than at the faster speed, 1.5 hours at 20 kilometres per hour, so her average speed is pulled below 15 kilometres per hour.

AIGEN_grade5_4c99bde9-c14b-4e70-aa8f-939.q: Kavita and her mother are going by bus from Pune to Mahabaleshwar for a weekend trip. The bus travels at 60 kilometres per hour for the first 45 minutes on the highway, then slows down to 30 kilometres per hour for the next 40 minutes through the ghat roads, and finally crawls at 15 kilometres per hour for the last 20 minutes through the town. What is the average speed of the bus for the entire journey?
hints: Remember: average speed equals total distance divided by total time. You'll need to find the distance covered in each part separately!

First convert each time from minutes to hours: 45 minutes equals three quarters of an hour, 40 minutes equals two thirds of an hour, 20 minutes equals one third of an hour. Then use Distance equals Speed times Time for each part.

Here's a similar problem. A car goes at 40 kilometres per hour for 30 minutes, covering 20 kilometres, and then at 20 kilometres per hour for 90 minutes, covering 30 kilometres. Total distance equals 20 plus 30, which is 50 kilometres. Total time equals 30 plus 90, which is 120 minutes, or 2 hours. Average speed equals 50 divided by 2, which is 25 kilometres per hour.
steps: Convert each time period from minutes to hours. 45 minutes equals 45 divided by 60, which is three quarters of an hour, 40 minutes equals 40 divided by 60, which is two thirds of an hour, 20 minutes equals 20 divided by 60, which is one third of an hour.
Find the distance covered in each part using Distance equals Speed times Time. D 1 equals 60 times three quarters, which is 45 kilometres.
Distance for the second part: D 2 equals 30 times two thirds, which is 20 kilometres.
Distance for the third part: D 3 equals 15 times one third, which is 5 kilometres.
Find the total distance and total time. Total distance equals 45 plus 20 plus 5, which is 70 kilometres.
Total time: three quarters plus two thirds plus one third, which is three quarters plus 1, which is 7 over 4 hours, or 1 hour 45 minutes.
Calculate the average speed. Average speed equals 70 divided by 7 over 4, which is 70 times 4 over 7, which is 40 kilometres per hour.

AIGEN_grade5_57d787f5-2ed4-4fc2-9026-dac.q: Deepa and her family are traveling by car from Jaipur to Udaipur for a wedding. The total distance is 400 kilometres. They drive at 80 kilometres per hour for the first 2 hours, then stop for chai for 30 minutes, and then continue the remaining distance at 60 kilometres per hour. How long does the entire journey take, including the chai break?
hints: Break the problem into parts: find the distance covered in the first part, then figure out how far is left, then find the time for the second part. Don't forget the chai break!
First, calculate the distance covered in the first 2 hours: Distance equals Speed times Time, which is 80 times 2, which is 160 kilometres.

Here's a similar problem: A bus covers 300 kilometres total. It goes at 50 kilometres per hour for 2 hours, covering 100 kilometres, stops for 15 minutes, then travels the remaining 200 kilometres at 40 kilometres per hour, taking 5 hours. Total time equals 2 hours plus 0.25 hours plus 5 hours, which is 7 hours 15 minutes.
steps: Find the distance covered in the first part of the journey. Distance 1 equals 80 times 2, which is 160 kilometres.
Find the remaining distance after the first part. Remaining equals 400 minus 160, which is 240 kilometres.
Find the time taken to cover the remaining 240 kilometres at 60 kilometres per hour. Time 2 equals 240 divided by 60, which is 4 hours.
Add up all the times: driving part 1 plus chai break plus driving part 2. Total equals 2 plus 0.5 plus 4, which is 6.5 hours, which is 6 hours 30 minutes.

AIGEN_grade5_597a64d3-34f5-4bb7-8a42-f7d.q: Aarav is riding his bicycle to his friend's house for a Diwali party. He rides at 10 kilometres per hour for the first 30 minutes, and then slows down to 6 kilometres per hour for the next 20 minutes because of a crowded market area. What is the total distance Aarav covers to reach his friend's house?
hints: Remember, the times are given in minutes, you'll need to convert them to hours before using the speed formula!
Convert 30 minutes to hours: 30 divided by 60 equals 0.5 hours. Now use Distance equals Speed times Time for each part of the journey.

Here's a similar problem. If someone walks at 8 kilometres per hour for 15 minutes, and then at 4 kilometres per hour for 30 minutes, the first distance is 8 times 15 over 60, which is 8 times 0.25, or 2 kilometres. The second is 4 times 30 over 60, which is 4 times 0.5, or 2 kilometres. That gives a total of 4 kilometres.
steps: Convert the times from minutes to hours. 30 minutes equals 30 divided by 60, which is 0.5 hours, 20 minutes equals 20 divided by 60, which is one third of an hour.
Find the distance covered in the first part using Distance equals Speed times Time. d 1 equals 10 times 0.5, which is 5 kilometres.
Find the distance covered in the second part. d 2 equals 6 times one third, which is 2 kilometres.
Add both distances to get the total distance. d total equals 5 plus 2, which is 7 kilometres.

AIGEN_grade5_6c21fe21-0dd5-461b-9280-a9c.q: Vikram is training for a school cricket tournament. Every morning, he jogs from his home to the cricket ground and then walks back home along the same route. He jogs at 8 kilometres per hour and walks back at 4 kilometres per hour. If the cricket ground is 4 kilometres away from his home, how much total time does Vikram spend traveling, going and coming back?
hints: Think about the two parts of the journey separately, the time going and the time coming back. Then add them up!
Use Time equals Distance divided by Speed for each part. The distance each way is 4 kilometres.

Here's a similar problem. Someone cycles 6 kilometres to a shop at 6 kilometres per hour, and walks back the same 6 kilometres at 3 kilometres per hour. Cycling time equals 6 divided by 6, which is 1 hour, and walking time equals 6 divided by 3, which is 2 hours. Total equals 1 plus 2, which is 3 hours.
steps: Find the time Vikram takes to jog to the cricket ground. Jogging time equals Distance divided by Speed, which is 4 divided by 8, which is 0.5 hours, which is 30 minutes.
Find the time Vikram takes to walk back home. Walking time equals 4 divided by 4, which is 1 hour, which is 60 minutes.
Add both times to get the total traveling time. Total time equals 30 plus 60, which is 90 minutes, which is 1 hour 30 minutes.

AIGEN_grade5_6ce388ca-8012-4430-aaed-00b.q: Deepa and her brother Arjun live in Mysore and are cycling to their grandmother's house in a nearby village for Sankranti. The total distance is 24 kilometres. Deepa starts at 8:00 a m and cycles at a constant speed of 8 kilometres per hour. Arjun starts 30 minutes later at 8 30 a m but cycles faster at 12 kilometres per hour. At what time does Arjun catch up with Deepa, and how far are they from grandmother's house at that moment?
options: 9 30 a m, and they are 6 kilometres away
9 30 a m, and they are 12 kilometres away
9:00 a m, and they are 16 kilometres away
10:00 a m, and they are 12 kilometres away
hints: Think about how far ahead Deepa is when Arjun starts, and then figure out how quickly Arjun closes that gap.
In 30 minutes, Deepa covers 8 times 0.5, which is 4 kilometres. Now Arjun gains on her at a rate of 12 minus 8 kilometres per hour. How long does it take him to close a 4-kilometre gap?

Similar problem: If car A starts at noon going 30 kilometres per hour and car B starts at 12 30 p m going 45 kilometres per hour, then A has a 15-kilometre head start. B gains at 15 kilometres per hour, so B catches A in 15 divided by 15, which is 1 hour, that is, at 1 30 p m. At that point, B has traveled 45 times 1, which is 45 kilometres from the start.
steps: Find Deepa's head start. She cycles for 30 minutes, 0.5 hours, before Arjun begins. Head start equals 8 times 0.5, which is 4 kilometres.
Find the relative speed, how fast Arjun closes the gap. Relative speed equals 12 minus 8, which is 4 kilometres per hour.
Find how long it takes Arjun to close the 4-kilometre gap. Time equals 4 divided by 4, which is 1 hour.
Since Arjun starts at 8 30 a m and takes 1 hour to catch up, he catches Deepa at 9 30 a m.
Find how far from the start they are when Arjun catches up. Arjun has cycled for 1 hour at 12 kilometres per hour. Distance from start equals 12 times 1, which is 12 kilometres.
Let's verify: Deepa has cycled for 1.5 hours at 8 kilometres per hour. 8 times 1.5 equals 12 kilometres.
Distance from grandmother's house equals total distance minus distance covered. 24 minus 12 equals 12 kilometres away.
So Arjun catches Deepa at 9 30 a m, and they are 12 kilometres from grandmother's house!

AIGEN_grade5_71d92ff4-e747-4f87-84f7-ea9.q: Kabir and his dad are going by car from Jaipur to a dhaba, roadside restaurant, that is 120 kilometres away. They drive at 60 kilometres per hour for the first half of the distance, but then hit traffic and slow down to 40 kilometres per hour for the remaining half of the distance. How long does the entire trip take?
hints: Think carefully, 'half the distance' means you need to find the time for each 60-kilometre part separately, then add them up!
First half: Time equals Distance divided by Speed, which is 60 divided by 60. Now do the same for the second half.

Here's a similar problem: A cyclist rides 40 kilometres at 20 kilometres per hour, then 40 kilometres at 10 kilometres per hour. Time for first part equals 40 divided by 20, which is 2 hours. Time for second part equals 40 divided by 10, which is 4 hours. Total time equals 6 hours. See how we split it up?
steps: Find half the total distance. 120 divided by 2 equals 60 kilometres.
Find the time for the first 60 kilometres at 60 kilometres per hour. Time 1 equals 60 divided by 60, which is 1 hour.
Find the time for the second 60 kilometres at 40 kilometres per hour. Time 2 equals 60 divided by 40, which is 1.5 hours, which is 1 hour 30 minutes.
Add both times together to get the total trip time. Total Time equals 1 plus 1.5, which is 2.5 hours, which is 2 hours 30 minutes.

AIGEN_grade5_760c2d33-3b78-477f-901a-993.q: Ravi and his grandfather are taking a boat ride during Onam celebrations in Kerala. The boat travels downstream at 18 kilometres per hour for 40 minutes to reach a temple. After offering prayers for 30 minutes, they return upstream along the same route at 12 kilometres per hour. What is their average speed for the entire journey, excluding the time spent at the temple?
hints: Think carefully: average speed equals total distance divided by total travel time. Don't just average the two speeds!
First, find the distance traveled downstream using Speed times Time. Remember to convert 40 minutes into hours!

Here's a similar problem. A boat goes downstream at 30 kilometres per hour for 20 minutes, so it covers 10 kilometres. It returns the same 10 kilometres at 15 kilometres per hour, which takes 40 minutes. Total distance equals 20 kilometres, and total time equals 60 minutes, or 1 hour, so average speed equals 20 kilometres per hour.
steps: Find the distance traveled downstream. Speed equals 18 kilometres per hour, Time equals 40 minutes, which is two thirds of an hour. Distance equals 18 times two thirds, which is 12 kilometres.
The return trip covers the same distance of 12 kilometres upstream at 12 kilometres per hour. Find the time for the return trip. Return time equals 12 divided by 12, which is 1 hour.

Find the total distance and total travel time, we exclude the 30 minutes at the temple since the question says so. Total distance equals 12 plus 12, which is 24 kilometres, Total time equals two thirds plus 1, which is 5 over 3 hours.
Calculate the average speed! Average speed equals 24 divided by 5 over 3, which is 24 times 3 over 5, which is 72 divided by 5, which is 14.4 kilometres per hour.

AIGEN_grade5_7c4fc3bc-d48a-4421-952e-19b.q: Suresh and Priya live in the same colony in Bangalore. Every morning, Suresh jogs to a park that is 6 kilometres away. He jogs at 6 kilometres per hour to the park and walks back home at 4 kilometres per hour. Priya cycles to the same park and back. She takes exactly the same total time as Suresh, but she cycles at a constant speed both ways. What is Priya's cycling speed?
hints: Think about what 'average speed' means when the distance is the same both ways, it's not just the simple average of the two speeds!
First find the time Suresh takes to go to the park, 6 kilometres at 6 kilometres per hour, and the time he takes to come back, 6 kilometres at 4 kilometres per hour. Add them up!

Here's a similar problem. Someone cycles 30 kilometres at 15 kilometres per hour, and returns the same 30 kilometres at 10 kilometres per hour. Total time equals 2 plus 3, which is 5 hours, and total distance equals 60 kilometres. A friend who covers the same 60 kilometres in the same 5 hours at a steady speed travels at 60 divided by 5, which is 12 kilometres per hour.
steps: Find the time Suresh takes to jog to the park. Time 1 equals 6 divided by 6, which is 1 hour.
Find the time Suresh takes to walk back from the park. Time 2 equals 6 divided by 4, which is 1.5 hours.
Find Suresh's total time for the round trip. Total Time equals 1 plus 1.5, which is 2.5 hours.
Find the total distance for the round trip. Total Distance equals 6 plus 6, which is 12 kilometres.
Priya covers the same 12 kilometres in the same 2.5 hours at a constant speed. So her speed is: Priya's speed equals 12 divided by 2.5, which is 4.8 kilometres per hour.

So Priya cycles at 4.8 kilometres per hour! Notice this is not the simple average of 6 and 4, which would be 5. When distances are equal, we use the harmonic mean formula: 2 times a times b, divided by, open bracket, a plus b, close bracket. That is 2 times 6 times 4, divided by, open bracket, 6 plus 4, close bracket, which is 48 divided by 10, or 4.8.

AIGEN_grade5_7dad391b-e598-40db-bb55-790.q: Priya and her family are taking a houseboat trip through the backwaters of Kerala. The houseboat travels downstream, with the current, at 12 kilometres per hour for 1 hour 30 minutes to reach a temple. After spending some time there, they return upstream, against the current, along the same route at 8 kilometres per hour. Meanwhile, Priya's cousin Arjun rides a bicycle along the road connecting the same two points. The road distance is 20 kilometres, and Arjun cycles at 10 kilometres per hour. If Arjun starts his bicycle ride at the exact moment the houseboat begins its return, upstream, journey, who arrives first and by how many minutes?
options: They arrive at the same time
hints: First figure out the downstream distance using speed times time. Then calculate how long each person's return journey takes separately.

Downstream distance equals 12 kilometres per hour times 1.5 hours, which is 18 kilometres. Now find the time for the houseboat to travel 18 kilometres upstream at 8 kilometres per hour, and the time for Arjun to cycle 20 kilometres at 10 kilometres per hour.

Here's a similar problem: A boat goes 10 kilometres downstream at 5 kilometres per hour, taking 2 hours. It returns at 4 kilometres per hour, taking 10 divided by 4, which is 2.5 hours. A cyclist covers 12 kilometres at 6 kilometres per hour, taking 2 hours. The cyclist is faster by 0.5 hours, which is 30 minutes. See how we compared the two travel times?
steps: Find the downstream distance the houseboat covers. Distance equals 12 times 1.5, which is 18 kilometres.
Find the time for the houseboat to return upstream, 18 kilometres at 8 kilometres per hour. Time for the boat equals 18 divided by 8, which is 2.25 hours, which is 2 hours 15 minutes.
Find the time for Arjun to cycle the road distance, 20 kilometres at 10 kilometres per hour. Time for Arjun equals 20 divided by 10, which is 2 hours.
Both start at the same moment. Compare their travel times. 2.25 minus 2 equals 0.25 hours, which is 15 minutes.
Since Arjun takes 2 hours and the houseboat takes 2 hours 15 minutes, Arjun arrives first by 15 minutes!

AIGEN_grade5_8d081413-2efb-49c7-b56e-22c.q: Ankit is going by train from Delhi to Agra to visit the Taj Mahal. The train travels at 90 kilometres per hour for the first 1 hour and then slows down to 60 kilometres per hour for the next 30 minutes due to a signal stop. What is the average speed of the train for the entire journey?
hints: Remember: average speed equals total distance divided by total time. Don't just average the two speeds!
First, find the distance covered in each part separately. For the first part: distance equals 90 times 1. For the second part: remember 30 minutes equals 0.5 hours.

Here's a similar problem. A car goes at 30 kilometres per hour for 2 hours, and then at 60 kilometres per hour for 1 hour. Total distance equals 30 times 2, plus 60 times 1. That is 60 plus 60, which is 120 kilometres. Total time equals 2 plus 1, which is 3 hours. Average speed equals 120 divided by 3, which is 40 kilometres per hour.
steps: Find the distance covered in the first part of the journey. Distance 1 equals 90 times 1, which is 90 kilometres.
Convert 30 minutes to hours for the second part. 30 minutes equals 30 divided by 60, which is 0.5 hours.
Find the distance covered in the second part of the journey. Distance 2 equals 60 times 0.5, which is 30 kilometres.
Find the total distance and total time. Total distance equals 90 plus 30, which is 120 kilometres, Total time equals 1 plus 0.5, which is 1.5 hours.
Calculate the average speed using the formula: average speed equals total distance divided by total time. Average speed equals 120 divided by 1.5, which is 80 kilometres per hour.

AIGEN_grade5_8e29fe73-a781-43bf-be05-6d8.q: Kavya's family is driving from Pune to a hill station for a weekend trip. They drive at 60 kilometres per hour for the first 2 hours on the highway. Then, on the winding mountain roads, they slow down to 30 kilometres per hour for the next 1 hour. What is their average speed for the entire journey?
hints: Remember, average speed isn't just the average of the two speeds! You need to find total distance divided by total time.
First, calculate the distance covered in each part: Distance equals Speed times Time. Then add them up!

Here's a similar problem: A boy walks 8 kilometres per hour for 3 hours and 4 kilometres per hour for 2 hours. Total distance equals 8 times 3 plus 4 times 2, which is 24 plus 8, which is 32 kilometres. Total time equals 3 plus 2, which is 5 hours. Average speed equals 32 divided by 5, which is 6.4 kilometres per hour. Notice this is not just 8 plus 4, all divided by 2, which is 6!
steps: Find the distance covered on the highway. Distance 1 equals 60 times 2, which is 120 kilometres.
Find the distance covered on the mountain roads. Distance 2 equals 30 times 1, which is 30 kilometres.
Find the total distance for the entire journey. Total Distance equals 120 plus 30, which is 150 kilometres.
Find the total time for the entire journey. Total Time equals 2 plus 1, which is 3 hours.
Calculate the average speed using the formula: Average Speed equals Total Distance divided by Total Time. Average Speed equals 150 divided by 3, which is 50 kilometres per hour.

AIGEN_grade5_9abd6007-86c6-467f-b518-630.q: Ravi and his grandfather take a morning walk around a rectangular park every day. The park is 400 metres long and 200 metres wide. They walk along the boundary of the park at a speed of 3 kilometres per hour. How many minutes does it take them to complete one full round of the park?
hints: First, figure out the total distance around the park, its perimeter. Then think about converting units so that distance and speed use the same units!
The perimeter of a rectangle equals 2 times, open bracket, length plus width, close bracket. Calculate this in metres, then convert to kilometres before using the speed.

Here's a similar problem: A square garden has sides of 250 metres. Someone walks around it at 2 kilometres per hour. Perimeter equals 4 times 250, which is 1000 metres, which is 1 kilometre. Time equals 1 divided by 2, which is 0.5 hours, which is 30 minutes. See how we converted metres to kilometres first? Try the same approach!
steps: One full round is the boundary: two lengths and two breadths. 2 times, open bracket, 400 plus 200, close bracket, equals 1200.
Make the units match. 3 kilometres in 1 hour is 3000 metres in 60 minutes.
So they walk 50 metres every minute. 3000 divided by 60 equals 50.
Divide the distance by the metres walked each minute. 1200 divided by 50 equals 24.
One full round takes 24 minutes.

AIGEN_grade5_9f8bd7db-3343-405c-b559-a28.q: Ravi and his dad are going by train from Chennai to Bengaluru. The train departs at 7 30 a m. For the first part of the journey, the train travels at 60 kilometres per hour for 2 hours. Then it stops at a station for 30 minutes. After that, it travels the remaining distance at 90 kilometres per hour and reaches Bengaluru at 12 30 p m. What is the total distance from Chennai to Bengaluru on this route?
hints: First figure out how much total time the journey takes, then subtract the time spent in the first part and the stop to find how long the train travels at 90 kilometres per hour.
Start by calculating the total journey time: from 7 30 a m to 12 30 p m is how many hours?

Here's a similar problem: A bus leaves at 8:00 a m, travels at 40 kilometres per hour for 1 hour, stops for 15 minutes, then travels at 50 kilometres per hour and arrives at 10 15 a m. Total time equals 2 hours 15 minutes. Time at 50 kilometres per hour equals 2 hours 15 minutes minus 1 hour minus 15 minutes, which is 1 hour. Distance equals 40 times 1 plus 50 times 1, which is 40 plus 50, which is 90 kilometres.
steps: Find the total journey time from 7 30 a m to 12 30 p m. 12 30, minus 7 30, equals 5 hours.
Calculate the distance covered in the first part at 60 kilometres per hour for 2 hours. Distance 1 equals 60 times 2, which is 120 kilometres.
The train stops for 30 minutes, which is 0.5 hours. No distance is covered during this time.
Find the time spent traveling in the second part. Subtract the first part and the stop from the total time. Time 2 equals 5 minus 2 minus 0.5, which is 2.5 hours.
Calculate the distance covered in the second part at 90 kilometres per hour for 2.5 hours. Distance 2 equals 90 times 2.5, which is 225 kilometres.
Add both distances to get the total distance. Total equals 120 plus 225, which is 345 kilometres.

AIGEN_grade5_9fab80d7-4e4f-464f-bccd-390.q: During a school sports day in Bengaluru, Neha and Kavitha start running towards each other from opposite ends of a 600-metre straight track at the same time. Neha runs at 5 metres per second and Kavitha runs at 3 metres per second. When they meet, Neha immediately turns around and runs back to her starting point at 4 metres per second. What is the total time, in seconds, from the start until Neha returns to her starting point?
hints: First figure out when Neha and Kavitha meet, they're running towards each other, so their speeds add up!
Time to meet equals total distance, divided by Neha's speed plus Kavitha's speed. That is 600 divided by, open bracket, 5 plus 3, close bracket. Then find how far Neha ran in that time.

Here's a similar problem: Two friends start 400 metres apart, running towards each other at 6 metres per second and 4 metres per second. They meet after 400 divided by 10, which is 40 seconds. The first friend covered 6 times 40, which is 240 metres. If she then walks back at 3 metres per second, her return time is 240 divided by 3, which is 80 seconds. Total equals 40 plus 80, which is 120 seconds.
steps: Find the time for Neha and Kavitha to meet. They run towards each other, so their combined speed is 5 plus 3, which is 8 metres per second.
Time to meet equals Total distance divided by Combined speed. t 1 equals 600 divided by 8, which is 75 seconds.
Find how far Neha ran from her starting point before they met. Distance Neha ran equals 5 times 75, which is 375 metres.
Neha now turns around and runs 375 metres back to her starting point at 4 metres per second. t 2 equals 375 divided by 4, which is 93.75 seconds.
Total time equals time to meet plus time to return, which is 75 plus 93.75, which is 168.75 seconds.

AIGEN_grade5_a6765258-aa69-4276-8490-060.q: Priya is traveling by train from Chennai to Bengaluru for a cricket match. The train covers the first 120 kilometres at 60 kilometres per hour. Then it slows down due to a signal stop and covers the next 80 kilometres at 40 kilometres per hour. Finally, it speeds up and covers the last 100 kilometres at 50 kilometres per hour. Meanwhile, her friend Deepa takes a bus that travels the entire 300-kilometre distance at a constant speed and reaches at exactly the same time as Priya. What is the speed of Deepa's bus?
hints: Think about it this way, if both reach at the same time, Deepa's bus takes the same total time as Priya's train. Can you find the total time Priya's train takes?
Start by finding the time for each part of Priya's journey using Time equals Distance divided by Speed, then add them up.

Here's a similar problem: A car covers 40 kilometres at 20 kilometres per hour and 60 kilometres at 30 kilometres per hour. Total distance equals 100 kilometres. Time one equals 40 divided by 20, which is 2 hours, Time two equals 60 divided by 30, which is 2 hours. Total time equals 4 hours. If another car covers 100 kilometres in the same 4 hours, its speed equals 100 divided by 4, which is 25 kilometres per hour. Use the same approach for Priya's problem!
steps: Find the time for each part of Priya's train journey using Time equals Distance divided by Speed.
Part 1: Time equals 120 divided by 60, which is 2 hours.
Part 2: Time equals 80 divided by 40, which is 2 hours.
Part 3: Time equals 100 divided by 50, which is 2 hours.
Total time for Priya's journey equals 2 plus 2 plus 2, which is 6 hours.
Total distance equals 120 plus 80 plus 100, which is 300 kilometres.
Deepa covers the same 300 kilometres in the same 6 hours. So her speed equals 300 divided by 6, which is 50 kilometres per hour.

AIGEN_grade5_a7714f4e-8b4a-40fd-945e-db3.q: Priya cycles from her home to the library at 12 kilometres per hour and returns along the same route at 8 kilometres per hour. If the library is 24 kilometres away from her home, what is her average speed for the entire trip?
hints: Average speed isn't just the average of the two speeds! Think about total distance divided by total time.
First, find the time taken for each part of the trip: Time equals Distance divided by Speed.

Here's a similar problem. Ravi walks 18 kilometres at 6 kilometres per hour, and returns at 3 kilometres per hour. Time going equals 18 divided by 6, which is 3 hours. Time returning equals 18 divided by 3, which is 6 hours. Total distance equals 36 kilometres and total time equals 9 hours, so average speed equals 36 divided by 9, which is 4 kilometres per hour.
steps: Find the total distance for the round trip. Total distance equals 24 plus 24, which is 48 kilometres.
Find the time taken to go to the library. Time 1 equals 24 divided by 12, which is 2 hours.
Find the time taken to return home. Time 2 equals 24 divided by 8, which is 3 hours.
Find the total time for the entire trip. Total time equals 2 plus 3, which is 5 hours.
Calculate the average speed using Total Distance divided by Total Time. Average speed equals 48 divided by 5, which is 9.6 kilometres per hour.

AIGEN_grade5_a954701c-ebae-486b-be8d-2cf.q: Neha and her family are taking a road trip from Pune to Goa for a beach holiday. The total distance is 450 kilometres. They drive at 75 kilometres per hour for the first 3 hours on the expressway, then stop for a 30-minute chai break, and then drive the remaining distance at 50 kilometres per hour on the winding ghat roads. What is their average speed for the entire journey, excluding the chai break?
hints: Think carefully: average speed equals total distance divided by total driving time. First find how far they went on the expressway, then figure out the remaining distance and how long that took.
Start by finding the expressway distance: 75 kilometres per hour times 3 hours equals how many kilometres? Then subtract from 450 kilometres to get the ghat road distance.

Here's a similar problem: A cyclist rides 40 kilometres at 20 kilometres per hour, taking 2 hours, and then rides 20 kilometres at 10 kilometres per hour, taking 2 hours. Average speed equals 60 kilometres divided by 4 hours, which is 15 kilometres per hour. Notice we use total distance divided by total time, not the average of the two speeds!
steps: Find the distance covered on the expressway. 75 times 3 equals 225 kilometres.
Find the remaining distance for the ghat roads. 450 minus 225 equals 225 kilometres.
Find the time taken on the ghat roads. 225 divided by 50 equals 4.5 hours.
Find the total driving time, excluding the chai break. 3 plus 4.5 equals 7.5 hours.
Calculate the average speed using total distance divided by total driving time. 450 divided by 7.5 equals 60 kilometres per hour.

AIGEN_grade5_b1cb3843-2972-4747-99e6-6cf.q: Deepak and his family are traveling by train from Chennai to Bengaluru. The train departs at 6 15 a m. For the first part of the journey, the train covers 120 kilometres at 60 kilometres per hour. Then it stops at Jolarpettai station for 30 minutes. After that, the train covers the remaining 240 kilometres at 80 kilometres per hour. At what time does the train arrive in Bengaluru?
hints: Break the journey into three parts: the first stretch, the stop, and the second stretch. Find the time for each part separately, then add them all up!
Start by finding the time for the first 120 kilometres: time equals distance divided by speed, which is 120 divided by 60. How many hours is that?

Here's a similar problem: A bus leaves at 8:00 a m, travels 50 kilometres at 25 kilometres per hour, that's 2 hours, stops for 15 minutes, then travels 90 kilometres at 30 kilometres per hour, that's 3 hours. Total travel time equals 2 hours plus 0.25 hours plus 3 hours, which is 5 hours 15 minutes. Arrival equals 8:00 a m plus 5 hours 15 minutes, which is 1 15 p m.
steps: Find the time for the first part of the journey. Time 1 equals 120 divided by 60, which is 2 hours.
Note the stop at Jolarpettai station. Stop time equals 30 minutes, which is 0.5 hours.
Find the time for the second part of the journey. Time 2 equals 240 divided by 80, which is 3 hours.
Add up all the times to get the total journey time. Total time equals 2 plus 0.5 plus 3, which is 5.5 hours, which is 5 hours 30 minutes.
Add the total journey time to the departure time. 6 15 a m plus 5 hours 30 minutes equals 11 45 a m.
So the train arrives in Bengaluru at 11 45 a m!

AIGEN_grade5_b30339a8-4dda-4ae6-bd0f-f55.q: Aarav and his dad are taking a train from Delhi to Agra to visit the Taj Mahal. The train travels at 90 kilometres per hour for the first 40 minutes, then slows down through a busy section at 60 kilometres per hour for the next 30 minutes, and finally speeds up to 120 kilometres per hour for the last 20 minutes. What is the total distance covered by the train?
hints: Remember, the times are given in minutes, but the speeds are in kilometres per hour. You'll need to convert!
Convert each time from minutes to hours by dividing by 60. For example, 40 minutes equals 40 divided by 60 hours, which is two thirds of an hour.

Here's a similar problem: A car goes at 60 kilometres per hour for 30 minutes and then at 80 kilometres per hour for 15 minutes. Distance one equals 60 times 30 divided by 60, which is 60 times 0.5, which is 30 kilometres. Distance two equals 80 times 15 divided by 60, which is 80 times 0.25, which is 20 kilometres. Total equals 30 plus 20, which is 50 kilometres. Now try the same approach with three parts!
steps: Convert all times from minutes to hours. 40 minutes equals 40 divided by 60, which is two thirds of an hour, 30 minutes equals 30 divided by 60, which is half an hour, 20 minutes equals 20 divided by 60, which is one third of an hour.
Find the distance for each part using Distance equals Speed times Time. d 1 equals 90 times two thirds, which is 60 kilometres.
Distance for the second part: d 2 equals 60 times one half, which is 30 kilometres.
Distance for the third part: d 3 equals 120 times one third, which is 40 kilometres.
Add all three distances to get the total distance. Total equals 60 plus 30 plus 40, which is 130 kilometres.

AIGEN_grade5_b8e871d8-1266-48e3-a10a-c21.q: Farhan is delivering samosas on his bicycle for his uncle's shop. He rides 6 kilometres from the shop to the first customer's house at a speed of 12 kilometres per hour. Then he rides 4 kilometres from the first customer's house to the second customer's house at a speed of 8 kilometres per hour. What is Farhan's average speed for the entire trip?
hints: Average speed isn't just the average of the two speeds! Think about total distance and total time.
First, find the time taken for each part of the trip using Time equals Distance divided by Speed.

Here's a similar problem: If someone walks 3 kilometres at 6 kilometres per hour and then 3 kilometres at 3 kilometres per hour, the time for the first part is 3 divided by 6, which is 0.5 hours and the second part is 3 divided by 3, which is 1 hour. Total distance equals 6 kilometres, total time equals 1.5 hours, so average speed equals 6 divided by 1.5, which is 4 kilometres per hour.
steps: Find the time for the first part of the trip, shop to first customer. Time 1 equals 6 divided by 12, which is 0.5 hours, 30 minutes.
Find the time for the second part of the trip, first customer to second customer. Time 2 equals 4 divided by 8, which is 0.5 hours, 30 minutes.
Find the total distance and total time. Total distance equals 6 plus 4, which is 10 kilometres, Total time equals 0.5 plus 0.5, which is 1 hour.
Calculate the average speed using the formula: Average Speed equals Total Distance divided by Total Time. Average speed equals 10 divided by 1, which is 10 kilometres per hour.
So Farhan's average speed for the entire samosa delivery trip is 10 kilometres per hour!

AIGEN_grade5_bfca9ba2-08fe-452f-8f60-22e.q: Ravi and his grandfather take a boat ride during the Onam festival in Kerala. They travel downstream, with the current, at 18 kilometres per hour for 40 minutes to reach a temple. After the puja, they return upstream, against the current, along the same route at 12 kilometres per hour. How many minutes does the return trip take?
hints: First figure out how far the temple is, you know the speed and time for the downstream trip! Then use that distance for the return trip.
Convert 40 minutes to hours: 40 minutes equals 40 divided by 60, which is two thirds of an hour. Now find the distance using Distance equals Speed times Time.

Here's a similar problem. A cyclist rides at 15 kilometres per hour for 20 minutes to reach a park. 20 minutes is one third of an hour, so the park is 15 divided by 3, which is 5 kilometres away. She returns at 10 kilometres per hour, so the return takes 5 divided by 10, which is half an hour, or 30 minutes.
steps: Convert the downstream travel time from minutes to hours. 40 minutes equals 40 divided by 60, which is two thirds of an hour.
Find the distance to the temple using Distance equals Speed times Time. Distance equals 18 times two thirds, which is 12 kilometres.
The return trip covers the same 12 kilometres, but at the upstream speed of 12 kilometres per hour. Find the time. Time equals Distance divided by Speed, which is 12 divided by 12, which is 1 hour.
Convert the answer back to minutes. 1 hour equals 60 minutes.

AIGEN_grade5_cd0b4e43-222d-47fc-9a45-b46.q: During a school sports day, Priya and Kiran start running from the same point at the same time, but in opposite directions around a circular track that is 600 metres long. Priya runs at 5 metres per second and Kiran runs at 3 metres per second. After how many seconds will they meet for the third time?
hints: When two people run in opposite directions on a circular track, think about how fast the gap between them closes. Their speeds add up!

First find their combined speed, relative speed, when running in opposite directions: 5 plus 3 equals 8 metres per second. Then figure out how long it takes to cover 600 metres at that speed, that's when they meet the first time.

Similar problem: Two cyclists start from the same point going in opposite directions on a 400-metre circular track at 6 metres per second and 4 metres per second. Relative speed equals 10 metres per second. Time for first meeting equals 400 divided by 10, which is 40 seconds. Time for second meeting equals 2 times 40, which is 80 seconds. See the pattern?
steps: Since Priya and Kiran run in opposite directions, their relative speed is the sum of their speeds. 5 plus 3 equals 8 metres per second.
They meet each time the combined distance they've covered equals one full lap, 600 metres. So the time for the first meeting is: Time 1 equals 600 divided by 8, which is 75 seconds.
After each meeting, they continue running and will meet again after covering another 600 metres together. So meetings happen at regular intervals of 75 seconds.
Time for the third meeting: Time 3 equals 3 times 75, which is 225 seconds.

Let's verify: In 225 seconds, Priya covers 5 times 225, which is 1125 metres and Kiran covers 3 times 225, which is 675 metres. Total equals 1800 metres, which is 3 times 600 metres. They've covered exactly 3 laps together, meaning 3 meetings!

AIGEN_grade5_e0aab10d-53f6-4e15-b3c9-090.q: Rohan and his dad are taking a road trip from Chennai to Pondicherry. The total distance is 150 kilometres. They drive the first 60 kilometres at 40 kilometres per hour, then stop for chai for 30 minutes. After that, they drive the next 60 kilometres at 60 kilometres per hour. For the last 30 kilometres, they get stuck in traffic and drive at only 15 kilometres per hour. What is their average speed for the entire journey, including the chai stop?
hints: Average speed equals Total Distance divided by Total Time. Don't forget to include the chai break in the total time!
First, find the time taken for each segment using Time equals Distance divided by Speed. Then add all three travel times plus the 30-minute break.

Here's a similar problem: A cyclist rides 20 kilometres at 10 kilometres per hour, rests for 1 hour, then rides 10 kilometres at 5 kilometres per hour. Total distance equals 30 kilometres. Time for first part equals 20 divided by 10, which is 2 hours. Rest equals 1 hour. Time for second part equals 10 divided by 5, which is 2 hours. Total time equals 5 hours. Average speed equals 30 divided by 5, which is 6 kilometres per hour. Notice how the rest time pulls the average speed down!
steps: Find the time for the first segment: 60 kilometres at 40 kilometres per hour. t 1 equals 60 divided by 40, which is 1.5 hours.
The chai stop lasts 30 minutes, which is 0.5 hours.
Find the time for the second segment: 60 kilometres at 60 kilometres per hour. t 2 equals 60 divided by 60, which is 1 hour.
Find the time for the third segment: 30 kilometres at 15 kilometres per hour. t 3 equals 30 divided by 15, which is 2 hours.
Add up all the times including the chai break. t total equals 1.5 plus 0.5 plus 1 plus 2, which is 5 hours.
Total distance is 150 kilometres. Now calculate average speed. Average Speed equals 150 divided by 5, which is 30 kilometres per hour.
So Rohan and his dad's average speed for the entire journey is 30 kilometres per hour!

AIGEN_grade5_e5f256fe-aa46-48e5-bdb7-1a6.q: Rohan is going by auto-rickshaw from his house to the railway station. The auto travels at 15 kilometres per hour for the first 20 minutes through narrow lanes, and then speeds up to 30 kilometres per hour for the next 30 minutes on the main road. What is the total distance from Rohan's house to the railway station?
hints: Remember, the times are given in minutes, so you'll need to convert them to hours before using the speed formula!
Convert 20 minutes to hours: 20 divided by 60 equals one third of an hour. Now find the distance for the first part using Distance equals Speed times Time.

Here's a similar problem: A cyclist rides at 12 kilometres per hour for 30 minutes and then at 18 kilometres per hour for 20 minutes. Distance one equals 12 times 30 divided by 60, which is 12 times 0.5, which is 6 kilometres. Distance two equals 18 times 20 divided by 60, which is 18 times one third, which is 6 kilometres. Total equals 6 plus 6, which is 12 kilometres.
steps: Identify the two parts of the journey. Part 1: speed equals 15 kilometres per hour, time equals 20 minutes. Part 2: speed equals 30 kilometres per hour, time equals 30 minutes.
Convert the times from minutes to hours. 20 minutes equals 20 divided by 60, which is one third of an hour, 30 minutes equals 30 divided by 60, which is half an hour.
Find the distance for Part 1 using Distance equals Speed times Time. d 1 equals 15 times one third, which is 5 kilometres.
Find the distance for Part 2 using Distance equals Speed times Time. d 2 equals 30 times one half, which is 15 kilometres.
Add both distances to get the total distance. d equals 5 plus 15, which is 20 kilometres.
The total distance from Rohan's house to the railway station is 20 kilometres!

AIGEN_grade5_e6a88dda-9aac-4665-aedd-a8e.q: Kavya and her mother are traveling by car from Jaipur to Udaipur for a family wedding. The total distance is 420 kilometres. They drive at 60 kilometres per hour for the first 3 hours, then stop for lunch for 30 minutes, and then drive the remaining distance at 80 kilometres per hour. What is their average speed for the entire journey, excluding the lunch break?
hints: Average speed equals Total distance divided by Total travel time, don't count the lunch break! First figure out how far they drove in the first part, then find the remaining distance.

Start by finding the distance covered in the first part: Distance equals Speed times Time, which is 60 times 3, which is 180 kilometres. Then the remaining distance is 420 minus 180, which is 240 kilometres.

Here's a similar problem. A bus covers 300 kilometres in total. It goes at 50 kilometres per hour for 2 hours, covering 100 kilometres, then covers the remaining 200 kilometres at 100 kilometres per hour, taking 2 hours. Total travel time equals 2 plus 2, which is 4 hours. Average speed equals 300 divided by 4, which is 75 kilometres per hour.
steps: Find the distance covered in the first part of the journey. Distance 1 equals 60 times 3, which is 180 kilometres.
Find the remaining distance. Distance 2 equals 420 minus 180, which is 240 kilometres.
Find the time taken to cover the remaining distance at 80 kilometres per hour. Time 2 equals 240 divided by 80, which is 3 hours.
Find the total travel time, excluding the lunch break. Total time equals 3 plus 3, which is 6 hours.
Calculate the average speed. Average speed equals 420 divided by 6, which is 70 kilometres per hour.

AIGEN_grade5_eae4d773-e97d-467f-91eb-84a.q: Meera walks from her house to the market at 4 kilometres per hour and takes an auto-rickshaw back home along the same route at 20 kilometres per hour. If the total time for her round trip is 3 hours, how far is the market from her house?
hints: Think about it this way: she travels the same distance twice, once slowly and once quickly. Can you write the time for each part using Time equals Distance divided by Speed?
Let the distance to the market be d kilometres. Time walking equals d over 4 hours, Time by auto equals d over 20 hours. Their sum equals 3 hours.

Here's a similar problem. Someone cycles to a park at 6 kilometres per hour and back at 12 kilometres per hour, and the total time is 6 hours. G5A_MEASUREMENT_001.q: A carpenter saws a log 3 metres 60 centimetres long into pieces of 45 centimetres each. Every cut takes him 4 minutes, and he rests for 1 minute between one cut and the next. How long does the whole job take, from the start of the first cut to the end of the last cut?
hints: Find the number of pieces first. Then picture the log: how many cuts make that many pieces, and how many rests fall between the cuts?
Change 3 metres 60 centimetres to 360 centimetres and divide by 45 to find the number of pieces. The number of cuts is one less than the number of pieces.

A similar job: a 2 metre pole cut into 50 centimetre pieces gives 4 pieces. That needs 3 cuts, with 2 rests between them. At 5 minutes a cut and 2 minutes a rest, the time is 3 times 5 plus 2 times 2 equals 19 minutes.
steps: Change the length to centimetres: 3 metres 60 centimetres equals 360 centimetres.
Find the number of pieces. 360 divided by 45 equals 8.
The last piece is simply what remains, so 8 pieces need 7 cuts. Rests come only between cuts, so there are 6 rests.
Add the cutting time and the resting time: the job takes 34 minutes.

G5A_MEASUREMENT_002.q: Riya glues 8 strips of paper end to end to make one long strip. Each strip is 25 centimetres long, and at every join the two strips overlap by 15 millimetres. How long is the finished strip?
hints: Two things need care here: the two lengths are in different units, and the number of joins is not the number of strips.

A similar chain: 5 strips of 20 centimetres with a 10 millimetre overlap at each join. There are 4 joins, so the length is 5 times 200 minus 4 times 10 equals 960 millimetres, which is 96 centimetres.
steps: Work in millimetres: each strip is 250 millimetres, so 8 strips laid end to end would be 2000 millimetres.
8 strips in a row have 7 joins, and each join hides 15 millimetres.
Take away the hidden length. 2000 minus 7 times 15 equals 1895.
1895 millimetres is 189 centimetres 5 millimetres, so the finished strip is 189 centimetres 5 millimetres long.

G5A_MEASUREMENT_003.q: A rectangular garden is 12 metres long and 7 metres 50 centimetres wide. Posts are put all the way round its boundary, 1 metre 50 centimetres apart, with a post at every corner. How many posts are needed?
hints: Think of walking once round the whole boundary from one post to the next until you are back at the start.
Find the distance all the way round the garden in centimetres, then see how many gaps of 150 centimetres fit into it.
A similar garden: a square of side 6 metres with posts 2 metres apart. The boundary is 24 metres, so there are 24 divided by 2 equals 12 gaps and, because the boundary closes up, 12 posts.
steps: Change to centimetres: the garden is 1200 centimetres by 750 centimetres.
Find the distance all the way round. 2 times open bracket 1200 plus 750 close bracket, equals 3900.
Find the number of gaps. 3900 divided by 150 equals 26.
Going round a closed boundary, the last gap ends at the first post, so the number of posts equals the number of gaps: 26 posts.

G5A_MEASUREMENT_004.q: An empty drum can hold 100 litres. Every morning Ravi pours 40 litres of water into it, and every night 25 litres leak out. On which morning does the drum become full for the first time?
hints: The water level goes up and then down each day. Ask yourself at which moment of the day the drum holds the most.
Write the level after each morning and after each night for the first two days, and look at how the morning levels grow.
A similar drum: it holds 50 litres, gains 20 litres each morning and loses 10 litres each night. Morning levels are 20, 30, 40, 50, so it is full on the 4th morning, not the 5th.
steps: After each full day and night the drum gains 40 minus 25 equals 15 litres.
The level just after each morning's pouring is 40, then 55, then 70, then 85 litres on the first four mornings.
After the 4th night the drum holds 85 minus 25 equals 60 litres.
The next morning's 40 litres bring it to 100 litres, so the drum is full on the 5th morning.

G5A_MEASUREMENT_005.q: A bottle full of juice weighs 1 kilogram 350 grams. When half of the juice has been drunk, the bottle and the remaining juice weigh 800 grams. What does the empty bottle weigh?
hints: Compare the two weighings. What exactly was removed between the first and the second?
Write 1 kilogram 350 grams as 1350 grams. The drop from 1350 grams to 800 grams is the weight of half of the juice.
A similar bottle: full it weighs 900 grams, and with half the oil used it weighs 600 grams. Half the oil is 300 grams, all the oil is 600 grams, so the bottle is 900 minus 600 equals 300 grams.
steps: Write the first weight in grams: 1 kilogram 350 grams equals 1350 grams.
The weight that went away is half of the juice. 1350 minus 800 equals 550.
So all of the juice weighs twice as much. 2 times 550 equals 1100.
Take the juice away from the full bottle: the empty bottle weighs 250 grams.

G5A_MEASUREMENT_006.q: A plane leaves Mumbai when the clocks in Mumbai show 11 40 p m. It lands in Dubai when the clocks in Dubai show 1 25 a m. Dubai clocks are always 1 hour 30 minutes behind Mumbai clocks. How long was the flight?
hints: The two times were read on clocks in different cities. Before finding the gap, put both times on the same city's clock.

A similar trip: a plane leaves town P at 10:00 p m by P's clocks and lands in town Q at 11:00 p m by Q's clocks, and Q's clocks are 2 hours behind P's. In P's time it lands at 1:00 a m, so the flight took 3 hours.
steps: Change the landing time to Mumbai time: 1 25 a m in Dubai is 1 hour 30 minutes later in Mumbai, which is 2 55 a m.
From 11 40 p m to midnight is 20 minutes.
From midnight to 2 55 a m is 2 hours 55 minutes.
20 minutes and 2 hours 55 minutes make 3 hours 15 minutes, so the flight took 3 hours 15 minutes.

G5A_MEASUREMENT_007.q: Meena's watch gains 5 minutes in every real hour. She sets it to the right time at 6:00 a m. Later the same day her watch shows 7:00 p m. What is the real time then?
hints: The watch gains 5 minutes for each real hour that passes, so think about how far the watch moves during one real hour.
In one real hour the watch moves 65 minutes. Find how many minutes the watch has moved from 6:00 a m to 7:00 p m.

A similar watch gains 10 minutes every real hour and is set right at 8:00 a m. When it shows 3:00 p m it has moved 420 minutes, which is 420 divided by 70 equals 6 real hours, so the real time is 2:00 p m.
steps: From 6:00 a m to 7:00 p m the watch has moved 13 hours, which is 780 minutes.
In each real hour the watch moves 60 plus 5 equals 65 minutes.
Find how many real hours have passed. 780 divided by 65 equals 12.
12 real hours after 6:00 a m is 6:00 p m, so the real time is 6:00 p m.

G5A_MEASUREMENT_008.q: Buses leave a depot every 25 minutes. The first bus of the day leaves at 6 40 a m. How many buses leave the depot before 1:00 p m?

A similar depot: buses every 20 minutes, the first at 9:00 a m. Before 10 10 a m there are 70 minutes, which hold 3 whole gaps, so buses leave at 9:00, 9 20, 9 40 and 10:00: that is 4 buses.
steps: From 6 40 a m to 1:00 p m is 6 hours 20 minutes, which is 380 minutes.
See how many whole gaps of 25 minutes fit. 15 times 25 equals 375.
So the last bus before 1:00 p m leaves 375 minutes after the first, at 12 55 p m.
There are 15 gaps, and the first bus leaves at the start of the first gap, so 15 plus 1 equals 16 buses leave.

G5A_MEASUREMENT_009.q: A model of a tower is made so that 1 centimetre on the model stands for 6 metres of the real tower. The model is 15 centimetres tall. A second model of the same tower is made so that 1 centimetre stands for 4 metres. How tall is the second model?
hints: Both models show the same real tower. Find the one thing that does not change, and use it as a bridge between the two models.

steps: Find the real height from the first model. 15 times 6 equals 90.
The real tower is 90 metres tall, and in the second model each centimetre stands for 4 metres.
Find how many centimetres are needed. 90 divided by 4 equals 22.5.
22.5 centimetres is 22 centimetres 5 millimetres, so the second model is 22 centimetres 5 millimetres tall.

G5A_MEASUREMENT_010.q: A carpenter has 6 planks, each 2 metres long. He needs pieces that are exactly 35 centimetres long, and each piece must be cut from a single plank. What is the greatest number of pieces he can cut?
