A similar job: 4 rods of 100 centimetres cut into 40 centimetre pieces. One rod gives 2 pieces with 20 centimetres left over, so 4 rods give 4 times 2 equals 8 pieces, even though 400 divided by 40 is 10.
steps: Each plank is 200 centimetres long.
See how many whole pieces one plank gives. 5 times 35 equals 175.
One plank gives 5 pieces and has 25 centimetres left over, which is too short for another piece.
Six planks give six times as many, so the greatest number is 30 pieces.

G5A_MEASUREMENT_011.q: A sheet of card is 32 centimetres long and 22 centimetres wide. Asha cuts small rectangular cards from it, each 80 millimetres by 50 millimetres. All the cards are placed the same way round, with their edges along the edges of the sheet. What is the greatest number of cards she can cut?
hints: Whole cards must fit along the length and along the width. Think about rows and columns rather than area, and remember the card can be turned.
Write the card as 8 centimetres by 5 centimetres. With the 8 centimetre side along the 32 centimetre edge, find how many cards fit along each edge.

A similar sheet: 20 centimetres by 13 centimetres, with cards 6 centimetres by 4 centimetres. One way gives 3 along and 3 up, which is 9 cards; turned, it gives 5 along and 2 up, which is 10 cards. So the most is 10, although the areas suggest more.
steps: The card is 8 centimetres by 5 centimetres.
With the 8 centimetre side along the 32 centimetre edge: 4 cards fit along the length and 4 rows fit in the 22 centimetre width, which makes 16 cards.
Turned round, with the 5 centimetre side along the 32 centimetre edge: 6 cards fit along the length but only 2 rows fit in the width, which makes 12 cards.
The first way is better, so the greatest number of cards is 16.

G5A_MEASUREMENT_012.q: 3 mangoes and 2 guavas together weigh 1 kilogram 150 grams. 2 mangoes and 3 guavas together weigh 1 kilogram 50 grams. All the mangoes weigh the same and all the guavas weigh the same. What does one mango weigh?
hints: A mango and a guava do not weigh the same, so sharing equally will not do. Look at what you get by putting the two weighings together, and by comparing them.
Add the two weighings: you then have 5 mangoes and 5 guavas. What do one mango and one guava weigh together?

A similar puzzle: 2 apples and 1 pear weigh 500 grams, and 1 apple and 2 pears weigh 400 grams. Together that is 3 apples and 3 pears for 900 grams, so one of each is 300 grams. Swapping a pear for an apple adds 100 grams, so an apple is 200 grams and a pear is 100 grams.
steps: In grams the two weighings are 1150 grams and 1050 grams. Together, 5 mangoes and 5 guavas weigh 2200 grams, so one mango and one guava weigh 440 grams.
The first weighing has one mango in place of a guava and is 100 grams heavier, so a mango weighs 100 grams more than a guava.
Two mangoes weigh 440 grams and 100 grams more. 440 plus 100 equals 540.
Halve it: one mango weighs 270 grams.

G5A_MEASUREMENT_013.q: A candle 24 centimetres tall burns down by 3 millimetres every 5 minutes. It is lit at 10 50 a m. At what time will the candle be exactly 6 centimetres tall?
hints: Read carefully what the 6 centimetres is: the part that has burned, or the part that is still standing?
Find how much of the candle must burn away, and write it in millimetres so that it matches the 3 millimetres.

A similar candle: 10 centimetres tall, burning 2 millimetres every 3 minutes, lit at 11 30 a m. To be 4 centimetres tall it must lose 60 millimetres, which is 30 lots of 2 millimetres and takes 90 minutes, so the time is 1:00 p m.
steps: Find how much must burn away, in centimetres. 24 minus 6 equals 18.
18 centimetres is 180 millimetres. Find how many lots of 3 millimetres that is. 180 divided by 3 equals 60.
Each lot takes 5 minutes. 60 times 5 equals 300.
300 minutes is 5 hours, and 5 hours after 10 50 a m is 3 50 p m, so the candle is 6 centimetres tall at 3 50 p m.

G5A_MEASUREMENT_014.q: Asha's steps are 60 centimetres long and her father's steps are 90 centimetres long. They start with their heels on the same line and walk 36 metres in the same straight direction. Counting the starting line, at how many places do their heel marks fall on the same spot?
hints: Asha's heel lands on multiples of one number and her father's on multiples of another. Where can both land?
List Asha's first few marks, 60 centimetres, 120 centimetres, 180 centimetres, and her father's, 90 centimetres, 180 centimetres, to find the first spot they share after the start.

A similar walk: steps of 40 centimetres and 60 centimetres over 6 metres. The marks meet every 120 centimetres, at 0, 120, 240, 360, 480 and 600 centimetres. That is 600 divided by 120 equals 5 gaps, so 6 shared places.
steps: Asha's marks are at multiples of 60 centimetres and her father's at multiples of 90 centimetres. The first distance in both lists is 180 centimetres.
So their marks fall together every 180 centimetres. The walk is 36 metres, which is 3600 centimetres.
Find how many gaps of 180 centimetres there are. 3600 divided by 180 equals 20.
The shared marks are at the start of the first gap and at the end of every gap, so there are 20 plus 1 equals 21 places.

G5A_MEASUREMENT_015.q: Kiran drank half of the juice in a jug and then 150 millilitres more. Later his sister drank half of what was left and then 100 millilitres more. Now 200 millilitres of juice is left in the jug. How much juice was in the jug at the start?
hints: The end is known and the start is not, so begin from the 200 millilitres and undo each thing that happened, the latest first.
Just before the sister drank her last 100 millilitres, the jug held 200 plus 100 equals 300 millilitres. That 300 millilitres was half of what she found in the jug.
A similar story: Tara spent half her money and then 20 rupees more, and has 30 rupees left. Before the 20 rupees she had 50 rupees, and that was half, so she began with 100 rupees.
steps: Put back the sister's last 100 millilitres. 200 plus 100 equals 300.
That was half of what she found, so double it. 300 times 2 equals 600.
Put back Kiran's extra 150 millilitres. 600 plus 150 equals 750.
That was half of the juice at the start, so double it: the jug held 1500 millilitres, which is 1 litre 500 millilitres.

G5A_MEASUREMENT_016.q: A wall clock takes 6 seconds to strike 4 o'clock, timed from the first strike to the last. The gaps between strikes are always equal. How long does the clock take to strike 10 o'clock?
hints: The timing starts on the first strike and stops on the last. Think about what fills the time in between.
Draw 4 dots in a row for the 4 strikes and count the gaps between them. The 6 seconds are shared among those gaps.
A similar clock takes 8 seconds to strike 3 o'clock. Three strikes have 2 gaps, so a gap is 4 seconds. Striking 6 o'clock has 5 gaps and takes 5 times 4 equals 20 seconds.
steps: Four strikes have 3 gaps between them.
Find the length of one gap. 6 divided by 3 equals 2.
Ten strikes have 9 gaps between them.
Nine gaps of 2 seconds: the clock takes 18 seconds.

G5A_MEASUREMENT_017.q: A machine is switched on at 9 40 p m on Thursday and runs without stopping for exactly 75 hours. On which day and at what time does it stop?
hints: Break the 75 hours into whole days and some hours left over. Whole days bring you back to the same clock time.
72 hours is exactly 3 days. Find the day and time 3 days after Thursday 9 40 p m, then see what the remaining hours do.
A similar run: a pump starts at 10 30 p m on Monday and runs for 50 hours. 48 hours later it is Wednesday 10 30 p m, and 2 more hours pass midnight, so it stops on Thursday at half past midnight.
steps: Split the 75 hours into whole days and extra hours. 75 equals 3 times 24 plus 3.
Three days after Thursday 9 40 p m is Sunday 9 40 p m.
Three more hours: 2 hours 20 minutes reach midnight, when Monday begins, and 40 minutes remain.
So the machine stops on Monday at 12 40 a m.

G5A_MEASUREMENT_019.q: A sports camp runs every day from 25 January 2024 to 5 March 2024, counting both the first day and the last day. For how many days does the camp run?
hints: Count the days month by month, and look closely at the year before deciding how long February is.
In January the camp runs on the 25th, 26th, 27th, 28th, 29th, 30th and 31st. Count them, then think about February 2024.
A similar count: from 20 February 2020 to 3 March 2020, both days included. 2020 is a leap year, so February gives 10 days, 20th to 29th, and March gives 3, which is 13 days.
steps: January: from the 25th to the 31st, both included, is 7 days.
February: 2024 can be divided exactly by 4, so it is a leap year and February has 29 days.
March: from the 1st to the 5th is 5 days.
Add the three parts: the camp runs for 41 days.

G5A_MEASUREMENT_020.q: A pile of 200 sheets of paper is 1 centimetre 6 millimetres thick. A book made of this paper has 350 numbered pages, with one page on each side of every sheet, and two covers that are each 1.5 millimetres thick. How thick is the book?
hints: Pages and sheets are not the same thing. Decide how many sheets of paper the book really has before working out any thickness.
Each sheet has a page on its front and a page on its back, so halve 350 to find the number of sheets. Then compare that with the pile of 200 sheets.
A similar book: 100 sheets make a pile 9 millimetres thick. A book of 400 pages has 200 sheets, which are 18 millimetres thick, and two covers of 1 millimetre each bring it to 20 millimetres.
steps: Find the number of sheets in the book. 350 divided by 2 equals 175.
The pile of 200 sheets is 16 millimetres thick, so 25 sheets are 2 millimetres thick.
175 sheets are 7 lots of 25 sheets. 7 times 2 equals 14.
Add the two covers: the book is 17 millimetres thick.

G5A_MEASUREMENT_021.q: Two clocks are set to the right time at 12 noon. One gains 3 minutes every hour and the other loses 2 minutes every hour. What time does the fast clock show when the two clocks are exactly 1 hour apart for the first time?
hints: Think about how quickly the two clocks move apart from each other, then about what the question finally asks you to read.
Each hour one clock goes 3 minutes ahead and the other falls 2 minutes behind, so the gap between them grows by 5 minutes an hour.

A similar pair, set right at 6:00 a m: one gains 4 minutes an hour and one loses 1 minute an hour. They are 20 minutes apart after 20 divided by 5 equals 4 hours, at a real time of 10:00 a m, when the fast clock shows 10 16 a m.
steps: Find how fast the gap between the clocks grows each hour. 3 plus 2 equals 5.
Find how many hours it takes for the gap to reach 60 minutes. 60 divided by 5 equals 12.
12 hours after 12 noon the real time is 12 midnight.
By then the fast clock has gained 36 minutes, so it shows 12 36 a m.

G5A_MEASUREMENT_022.q: A bottle holds 75 millilitres of cough syrup. Anu takes 5 millilitres every morning and 5 millilitres every night. Her first dose is on Monday night. When does she take the last dose from the bottle?
hints: Count doses rather than days, and notice that the first day is not a full day of medicine.
Find how many 5 millilitre doses the bottle holds. One of them is used on the first Monday night, and after that she takes two every day.

A similar bottle holds 35 millilitres and gives 7 doses of 5 millilitres. If the first dose is on Friday night, the other 6 doses fill Saturday, Sunday and Monday, so the last dose is on Monday night.
steps: Find the number of doses in the bottle. 75 divided by 5 equals 15.
The first dose is on Monday night, which leaves 14 doses.
At 2 doses a day, find how many whole days they last. 14 divided by 2 equals 7.
Those 7 days are Tuesday to the next Monday, and each ends with a night dose, so the last dose is on the next Monday night.

G5A_SPEED_001.q: Asha cycles at a steady speed of 12 kilometres per hour. How far does she cycle in 3 hours?
hints: Speed tells you how far something goes in one hour. Distance is speed multiplied by time.
Asha goes 12 kilometres in the first hour, 12 kilometres in the second and 12 kilometres in the third.
A similar one: a cyclist going 10 kilometres per hour for 2 hours covers 10 times 2 equals 20 kilometres.
steps: Distance is speed multiplied by time.
Multiply 12 kilometres per hour by 3 hours. 12 times 3 equals 36.
Asha cycles 36 kilometres.

G5A_SPEED_002.q: A snail crawls 5 centimetres every minute. How far does it crawl in 8 minutes?
hints: The snail covers the same distance every minute. Distance is speed multiplied by time.
The speed is 5 centimetres each minute and the time is 8 minutes. Multiply them.
A similar one: an ant that walks 4 centimetres every minute walks 4 times 6 equals 24 centimetres in 6 minutes.
steps: Distance is speed multiplied by time.
Multiply 5 centimetres each minute by 8 minutes. 5 times 8 equals 40.
The snail crawls 40 centimetres.

G5A_SPEED_003.q: Ravi swims at a steady speed of 2 metres every second. How long does he take to swim 50 metres?
hints: Time is distance divided by speed.
Ask how many lots of 2 metres fit into 50 metres. Each lot takes 1 second.
A similar one: a swimmer who covers 2 metres every second swims 30 metres in 30 divided by 2 equals 15 seconds.
steps: Time is distance divided by speed.
Divide 50 metres by 2 metres each second. 50 divided by 2 equals 25.
Ravi takes 25 seconds.

G5A_SPEED_004.q: Rahul walks at a steady speed of 4 kilometres per hour. How long does he take to walk 12 kilometres?
hints: Time is distance divided by speed.
Ask how many lots of 4 kilometres fit into 12 kilometres. Each lot takes 1 hour.
A similar one: walking at 5 kilometres per hour, a walk of 10 kilometres takes 10 divided by 5 equals 2 hours.
steps: Time is distance divided by speed.
Divide 12 kilometres by 4 kilometres per hour. 12 divided by 4 equals 3.
Rahul takes 3 hours.

G5A_SPEED_005.q: A boat travels 45 kilometres along a river in 3 hours at a steady speed. What is the speed of the boat?
hints: Speed is the distance covered in one unit of time. Speed is distance divided by time.
The boat covers 45 kilometres in 3 hours. Share 45 kilometres equally among the 3 hours.
A similar one: a boat that travels 40 kilometres in 4 hours has a speed of 40 divided by 4 equals 10 kilometres per hour.
steps: Speed is distance divided by time.
Divide 45 kilometres by 3 hours. 45 divided by 3 equals 15.
The speed of the boat is 15 kilometres per hour.

G5A_SPEED_006.q: A horse gallops 600 metres in 2 minutes at a steady speed. How many metres does it gallop in one minute?
hints: The distance covered in one minute is the speed. Speed is distance divided by time.
The horse covers 600 metres in 2 minutes. Share 600 metres equally between the 2 minutes.
A similar one: a horse that gallops 800 metres in 2 minutes covers 800 divided by 2 equals 400 metres in one minute.
steps: Speed is distance divided by time.
Divide 600 metres by 2 minutes. 600 divided by 2 equals 300.
The horse gallops 300 metres in one minute.

G5A_SPEED_007.q: A toy car moves 10 centimetres every second. How long does it take to move 80 centimetres?
hints: Time is distance divided by speed.
Ask how many lots of 10 centimetres fit into 80 centimetres. Each lot takes 1 second.
A similar one: a toy car that moves 10 centimetres every second takes 60 divided by 10 equals 6 seconds to move 60 centimetres.
steps: Time is distance divided by speed.
Divide 80 centimetres by 10 centimetres each second. 80 divided by 10 equals 8.
The toy car takes 8 seconds.

G5A_SPEED_008.q: Kavya walks 100 metres in 50 seconds at a steady speed. What is her speed in metres per second?
hints: Speed is the distance covered in one unit of time. Speed is distance divided by time.
Kavya covers 100 metres in 50 seconds. Share 100 metres equally among the 50 seconds.
A similar one: someone who walks 90 metres in 30 seconds has a speed of 90 divided by 30 equals 3 metres per second.
steps: Speed is distance divided by time.
Divide 100 metres by 50 seconds. 100 divided by 50 equals 2.
Kavya's speed is 2 metres per second.

G5A_SPEED_009.q: A lorry travels at a steady speed of 40 kilometres per hour for 5 hours. What distance does it cover?
hints: Speed tells you how far something goes in one hour. Distance is speed multiplied by time.
The lorry goes 40 kilometres in every one of the 5 hours. Multiply 40 by 5.
A similar one: a lorry going 30 kilometres per hour for 4 hours covers 30 times 4 equals 120 kilometres.
steps: Distance is speed multiplied by time.
Multiply 40 kilometres per hour by 5 hours. 40 times 5 equals 200.
The lorry covers 200 kilometres.

G5A_SPEED_010.q: Four friends each cycled for exactly 1 hour. Ravi covered 14 kilometres, Sana covered 11 kilometres, Tina covered 16 kilometres and Uday covered 9 kilometres. Who cycled at the greatest speed?
hints: When everyone travels for the same time, the fastest is the one who goes the furthest.
Each friend cycled for 1 hour, so the distance each one covered is also the speed in kilometres per hour. Compare the four distances.
A similar one: in 1 hour Meena walks 5 kilometres and Arjun walks 4 kilometres. Meena covers more in the same time, so Meena is faster.
steps: All four cycled for the same time, 1 hour, so compare the distances.
The distances are 14 kilometres, 11 kilometres, 16 kilometres and 9 kilometres. The greatest is 16 kilometres.
So Tina cycled at the greatest speed.
